boundaries_en: Abrogation bears on the ruling, not on the text: an ayah whose ruling is abrogated stands in the mushaf as it is.
The relation is disputed in many places, so it is bound to its source and never presented as agreed upon.
abrogation.definition_en: The lifting of a legal ruling by a later legal proof. In the Quran it is studied by relating an abrogating ayah to an abrogated one.
abrogation.purpose_en: Used to represent the relation between two ayahs, one abrogating and one abrogated: a relation between two places in the text, not a property of a single ayah.

asbab_al_nuzul.definition_en: The events or questions that an ayah, or several ayahs, was revealed to address or to rule on.
asbab_al_nuzul.purpose_en: Used to attach the narrations and the material about an ayah's occasion of revelation to the ayah itself.

boundaries_en: Its position on a page or a line belongs to the mushaf and its layout, not to the identity of the ayah.
The ayah ending is the close of the ayah, not the ayah.
ayah.definition_en: A unit of the Quranic text falling within a surah and having determined boundaries. Its number, and some of its boundaries, may differ from one ayah numbering system to another.
ayah.purpose_en: Used as the basic unit for referring to the Quranic text, and for attaching translations, tafsir, recitations, analyses and other data to a specific place in the Quran.

boundaries_en: The count belongs to the surah under a numbering system, not to the mushaf.
ayah_count.definition_en: The number of ayahs in a surah under a given numbering system; it may differ from one system to another as the counted fasilahs differ.
ayah_count.note_en: The code name follows `ayah_numbering_*` and the registry's name, not a derivation of «عَدَد الآيَات»; the concept is one of modelling, though the count of ayahs has its origin in the science of counting.
ayah_count.purpose_en: Used to check references and surah boundaries and to build indexes; it is read from the registry of counts, not computed from one text.

boundaries_en: The fasilah is the ayah's ending as a matter of the text; the ayah mark is the sign drawn in the mushaf for it.
ayah_ending.definition_en: The close of an ayah or a passage as a matter of its composition; some scholars define it as the ayah's last word.
ayah_ending.purpose_en: Used in studies and datasets concerned with ayah endings and Quranic composition. It is never used as a synonym for `ayah`.

boundaries_en: A maqta belongs to the layout of one mushaf and is no part of the identity of the ayah.
A maqta is not a word: it may be a word, several words, or part of a word where the break falls inside one.
ayah_fragment.definition_en: What appears of one ayah on one line of a page of a given mushaf; an ayah that runs over two lines is two maqtas.
ayah_fragment.purpose_en: Used as the unit of display and tagging in the page layout, because an ayah does not keep to a line nor a line to an ayah; alignment and highlighting in a drawn mushaf are built on it.

boundaries_en: The key is a reference, not an identity: changing the numbering system changes the key and not the ayah.
The key is not the running number of the ayah across the whole mushaf.
ayah_key.definition_en: A textual identifier of an ayah joining its surah number and its number within it with a colon, in the form `2:255`; it is read only in the light of the ayah numbering system it rests on.
ayah_key.purpose_en: Used as the key that joins data sources and carries a reference to an ayah between APIs and files; binding it to a numbering system stops one key from pointing at two places.

boundaries_en: The mark is something drawn in the mushaf; the ayah ending is the close of the ayah as a matter of the text itself.
The number inside the circle follows an ayah numbering system and is not part of the mark.
ayah_mark.definition_en: The circle separating one ayah from the next. It is placed at the ayah's end and, in most mushafs, carries its number.
ayah_mark.purpose_en: Used to mark an ayah's boundary in the written text; it is the sign from which a renderer or an analyser reads where an ayah ends and what its number is.

ayah_numbering_basri.definition_en: The Basran numbering system, transmitted from Asim al-Jahdari and the Basran authorities before him.
ayah_numbering_basri.note_en: The code is `basri` alone, because a value's name is unique within its classification, not across the dictionary (§14): a column holds one classification's values, so `makki` here is never confused with `makki` in `revelation_classification`. The entry's id is `ayah_numbering_basri`, the parent's name plus the code, so that two entries sharing a name have different addresses. The code is not derived from «العَدّ» because that gives `add`, an English verb. The reasoning is in the decision record.
ayah_numbering_basri.purpose_en: Used as a value of the ayah numbering system, so that a mushaf or dataset states which numbering its ayah numbers and boundaries follow, and positions can be mapped between systems.

ayah_numbering_dimashqi.definition_en: The Damascene numbering system, transmitted from Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Dhimari from Ibn Amir; also called the Shami numbering.
ayah_numbering_dimashqi.note_en: The code is `dimashqi` alone, because a value's name is unique within its classification, not across the dictionary (§14): a column holds one classification's values, so `makki` here is never confused with `makki` in `revelation_classification`. The entry's id is `ayah_numbering_dimashqi`, the parent's name plus the code, so that two entries sharing a name have different addresses. The code is not derived from «العَدّ» because that gives `add`, an English verb. The reasoning is in the decision record.
ayah_numbering_dimashqi.purpose_en: Used as a value of the ayah numbering system, so that a mushaf or dataset states which numbering its ayah numbers and boundaries follow, and positions can be mapped between systems.

ayah_numbering_kufi.definition_en: The Kufan numbering system, transmitted from Hamzah al-Zayyat from Ibn Abi Layla from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami from Ali ibn Abi Talib. It is the numbering most printed mushafs follow today.
ayah_numbering_kufi.note_en: The code is `kufi` alone, because a value's name is unique within its classification, not across the dictionary (§14): a column holds one classification's values, so `makki` here is never confused with `makki` in `revelation_classification`. The entry's id is `ayah_numbering_kufi`, the parent's name plus the code, so that two entries sharing a name have different addresses. The code is not derived from «العَدّ» because that gives `add`, an English verb. The reasoning is in the decision record.
ayah_numbering_kufi.purpose_en: Used as a value of the ayah numbering system, so that a mushaf or dataset states which numbering its ayah numbers and boundaries follow, and positions can be mapped between systems.

ayah_numbering_madani_first.definition_en: The earlier Madinan numbering system, that of Abu Jafar Yazid ibn al-Qaqa and Shaybah ibn Nassah.
ayah_numbering_madani_first.note_en: The code is `madani_first` alone, because a value's name is unique within its classification, not across the dictionary (§14): a column holds one classification's values, so `makki` here is never confused with `makki` in `revelation_classification`. The entry's id is `ayah_numbering_madani_first`, the parent's name plus the code, so that two entries sharing a name have different addresses. The code is not derived from «العَدّ» because that gives `add`, an English verb. The reasoning is in the decision record.
ayah_numbering_madani_first.purpose_en: Used as a value of the ayah numbering system, so that a mushaf or dataset states which numbering its ayah numbers and boundaries follow, and positions can be mapped between systems.

ayah_numbering_madani_last.definition_en: The later Madinan numbering system, that of Ismail ibn Jafar from Sulayman ibn Jammaz.
ayah_numbering_madani_last.note_en: The code is `madani_last` alone, because a value's name is unique within its classification, not across the dictionary (§14): a column holds one classification's values, so `makki` here is never confused with `makki` in `revelation_classification`. The entry's id is `ayah_numbering_madani_last`, the parent's name plus the code, so that two entries sharing a name have different addresses. The code is not derived from «العَدّ» because that gives `add`, an English verb. The reasoning is in the decision record.
ayah_numbering_madani_last.purpose_en: Used as a value of the ayah numbering system, so that a mushaf or dataset states which numbering its ayah numbers and boundaries follow, and positions can be mapped between systems.

ayah_numbering_makki.definition_en: The Makkan numbering system, transmitted from Ibn Kathir from Mujahid from Ibn Abbas from Ubayy ibn Kab.
ayah_numbering_makki.note_en: The code is `makki` alone, because a value's name is unique within its classification, not across the dictionary (§14): a column holds one classification's values, so `makki` here is never confused with `makki` in `revelation_classification`. The entry's id is `ayah_numbering_makki`, the parent's name plus the code, so that two entries sharing a name have different addresses. The code is not derived from «العَدّ» because that gives `add`, an English verb. The reasoning is in the decision record.
ayah_numbering_makki.purpose_en: Used as a value of the ayah numbering system, so that a mushaf or dataset states which numbering its ayah numbers and boundaries follow, and positions can be mapped between systems.

ayah_numbering_system.definition_en: A system that fixes the boundaries of the ayahs, their totals and their numbers, and certain questions about the basmalah, as transmitted by one of the schools of ayah counting.
ayah_numbering_system.purpose_en: Used to state which numbering system a mushaf's or a dataset's ayah numbers and boundaries follow.

boundaries_en: A timing is a property of the recording, not of the ayah, so it differs from one recitation to another.
Ayah-level timing is not word-level alignment.
ayah_timing.definition_en: A span of time in a recitation recording, given by a start and an end, corresponding to one ayah.
ayah_timing.purpose_en: Used to bind text to audio; following along while listening, jumping to an ayah, repeating it and clipping it all rest on it.

basmalah.definition_en: The formula «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» with which the surahs open, except surah al-Tawbah. It carries rulings and differences bound up with ayah counting.
basmalah.purpose_en: Used to identify the basmalah and to represent its position and its relation to the surah and to the ayah numbering system.

boundaries_en: A character is a unit of encoding; a letter is a linguistic unit, and one letter may be carried by more than one character.
A character is not a glyph: the glyph is produced by the font, the character is carried by the text.
character.definition_en: An abstract unit of text in a digital encoding; it need not correspond to a single linguistic letter.
character.purpose_en: Used where an offset, a length or a comparison must be exact: text-path tests, search indexes and the allowlist of permitted characters.

codepoint.definition_en: A numeric value defined by an encoding standard such as Unicode.
codepoint.purpose_en: Used where the exact encoding of a character or mark matters: normalisation rules, font mappings and the allowlist of permitted codepoints.

dammah.definition_en: The mark for the short vowel u on the letter.
dammah.purpose_en: Used as a value of harakah, so that a letter's pronunciation is read from it in analysis, rendering and teaching rather than from the shape of the mark.

disputed.definition_en: A surah or ayah that the accepted sources do not agree to classify as makki or madani.
disputed.purpose_en: Keeps disputed data from being forced into `makki` or `madani` without recording the disagreement.

boundaries_en: The division mark is a sign in the mushaf; the juz, the hizb and its quarters are divisions of the text it points to.
division_mark.definition_en: Marks the start of a juz, a hizb, or a half or quarter of one.
division_mark.note_en: `alamat_al_tahzib` was a separate entry defining the same thing; it was merged into this one.
division_mark.purpose_en: Used as a mark of the mushaf, so that rendering and analysis know where it sits and what it points to.

dot.definition_en: One dot, above or below, distinguishing a letter from the others that share its skeleton (ijam): baa, noon, jeem, khaa, dhaal.
dot.purpose_en: Used as a value of ijam, so that a letter is told apart from those sharing its skeleton in analysis and in search.

boundaries_en: This is a correspondence between two numbering systems, not a similarity of wording or a repetition of text.
equivalent_ayah.definition_en: The ayah in one numbering system that corresponds to an ayah in another. Their numbers may differ, because the systems divide the text at different points.
equivalent_ayah.purpose_en: Used to map ayah numbers across numbering systems, so that data built on one system is never compared with data built on another by number alone.

fathah.definition_en: The mark for the short vowel a on the letter.
fathah.purpose_en: Used as a value of harakah, so that a letter's pronunciation is read from it in analysis, rendering and teaching rather than from the shape of the mark.

boundaries_en: A font is a means of display; the rasm is a property of the written text itself.
A glyph is a shape inside a font; a letter is a unit of the text.
font.definition_en: A file carrying a set of glyphs and the rules for laying them out, used to render the text of a mushaf.
font.purpose_en: Used to record which font a digital mushaf depends on, since in many of them the text renders correctly in one font only, so letter codes, their shapes and line positions are tied to it.

boundaries_en: Ghunnah is an attribute of sound and not a ruling in itself: it accompanies idgham, ikhfa and iqlab and does not stand opposite them.
ghunnah.definition_en: A sound from the nasal cavity built into the body of noon and meem, in which the tongue plays no part; its length differs by ruling, fullest in the doubled and the merged letter, then in the concealed, then in the vowelless letter sounded clearly.
ghunnah.purpose_en: Used as an attribute tagging the places in the text where the ghunnah is held, such as the two doubled letters, idgham with ghunnah, ikhfa and iqlab, so that it is followed in colouring and instruction, and because its length is among what differs by tariq.

boundaries_en: A glyph is produced by the font; it is neither the letter nor the character, and one character may be drawn by many glyphs.
glyph.definition_en: The visual shape a font produces to represent a letter, a character, or a group of them.
glyph.purpose_en: Used for fonts, rasm, rendering and the placement of visual shapes.

grapheme.definition_en: A written unit that a user perceives as one unit, which may consist of more than one `codepoint`.
grapheme.purpose_en: Used for visual segmentation, editing and text selection, where the codepoint is not the right unit.

hadr.definition_en: Reciting quickly while keeping the letters, the vowels and the rules of delivery intact.
hadr.purpose_en: Used as a value of recitation pace, so that a recording or a teaching session is tagged by its pace and filtered by it.

hamzah.definition_en: Marks a fully realised hamzah (hamzat al-qat).
hamzah.purpose_en: Used as a value of the orthographic marks, so that software can tell where the rasm departs from the pronunciation.

hamzat_al_wasl.definition_en: Marks a connecting hamzah, dropped whenever the word is reached in continuation.
hamzat_al_wasl.purpose_en: Used as a value of the orthographic marks, so that software can tell where the rasm departs from the pronunciation.

harakah.definition_en: A mark fixing a letter's vowel, its absence or its doubling: fathah, dammah, kasrah, sukun and shaddah.
harakah.purpose_en: Used as the parent of the dabt marks that determine how the letter itself is pronounced.

hizb.definition_en: In the current division, half a juz, so that the Quran is 60 hizbs.
hizb.purpose_en: Used to represent the conventional divisions, navigation, and reading plans.

boundaries_en: Idgham is a ruling; mutamathilan, mutajanisan and mutaqariban are the relation between the two letters because of which it falls.
idgham.definition_en: Merging a vowelless letter into a vowelled letter after it so that the two become one doubled letter, whether the merging is complete or partial, with ghunnah or without it.
idgham.purpose_en: Used as a value of the tajwid ruling, so that a place in the text is tagged with it in analysis, colouring and instruction, and its kinds branch under it in the registry of rulings.

ijam.definition_en: The dotting that distinguishes a letter from the letters that share its written shape.
ijam.purpose_en: Used as the parent of the dot shapes, which are told apart by their number and position rather than by their function.

ikhfa.definition_en: Pronouncing a vowelless letter in a manner between izhar and idgham, without doubling and with the ghunnah kept: haqiqi in noon sakinah and tanwin before its 15 letters, and shafawi in meem sakinah before a baa.
ikhfa.purpose_en: Used as a value of the tajwid ruling, so that a place in the text is tagged with it in analysis, colouring and instruction, and its kinds branch under it in the registry of rulings.

imalah.definition_en: Marks the major imalah: a fathah pronounced leaning toward kasrah. In the riwayah of Hafs it occurs at one place only (11:41).
imalah.purpose_en: Used as a value of the qiraah marks, so that the reader is alerted to a particular delivery at its place.

instructional_ayah_repetition.definition_en: Repeating an ayah, or part of one, once or several times in a teaching pattern that helps the learner take it in and memorise it.
instructional_ayah_repetition.purpose_en: Used to describe a feature of a teaching recording in its own right, rather than leaving it implied inside `muallim`.

boundaries_en: Iqlab is a ruling of pronunciation; the small meem is the mark the mushaf draws it with.
iqlab.definition_en: Turning noon sakinah or tanwin into a meem, concealed with ghunnah, before a baa.
iqlab.purpose_en: Used as a value of the tajwid ruling, so that a place in the text is tagged with it in analysis, colouring and instruction, and its kinds branch under it in the registry of rulings.

irab.definition_en: The statement of the syntactic function of words, their case markers, and their relations within the construction.
irab.purpose_en: Used to attach syntactic analysis and grammatical functions to the words of an ayah.

ishmam.definition_en: Marks ishmam: the lips are rounded to hint at a dropped dammah, without any sound.
ishmam.purpose_en: Used as a value of the qiraah marks, so that the reader is alerted to a particular delivery at its place.

istiadhah.definition_en: Seeking refuge with Allah from the Shaytan before reciting the Quran.
istiadhah.purpose_en: Used to represent the istiadhah, its wordings, and its position relative to the start of a recitation.

boundaries_en: Izhar is a ruling standing opposite idgham and ikhfa, not the absence of a ruling: a place tagged with it is one where a cause was present and neither idgham nor ikhfa fell.
izhar.definition_en: Sounding a vowelless letter from its point of articulation with no added ghunnah, as noon sakinah and tanwin are sounded before the throat letters, and meem sakinah before any letter other than baa and meem.
izhar.purpose_en: Used as a value of the tajwid ruling, so that a place in the text is tagged with it in analysis, colouring and instruction, and its kinds branch under it in the registry of rulings.

juz.definition_en: One of the 30 parts of the well-known division of the mushaf, made to ease reading and completing it.
juz.purpose_en: Used for navigation, for organising reading, and for the schedules and plans built on the parts of the Quran.

kasrah.definition_en: The mark for the short vowel i on the letter.
kasrah.purpose_en: Used as a value of harakah, so that a letter's pronunciation is read from it in analysis, rendering and teaching rather than from the shape of the mark.

khatmah.definition_en: Reading the Quran in full, from its beginning to its end.
khatmah.purpose_en: Used to track completion plans, to record that a reading was finished, and to tie sessions to the course of one khatmah.

layout.definition_en: The visual arrangement of the text and its elements into pages, lines and positions within a given mushaf or view.
layout.purpose_en: Keeps visual data apart from the fixed textual structure of the Quran.

lemma.definition_en: The base dictionary form that an inflected word form is referred back to.
lemma.purpose_en: Used to gather the different inflected forms under one dictionary entry.

boundaries_en: A letter is a linguistic unit; a character is a unit of encoding, and one letter may be written with one character or more.
A letter is a unit of writing; harf al-mana is a part of speech.
letter.definition_en: A letter of the alphabet as a linguistic unit of writing.
letter.purpose_en: Used for data that deals with linguistic letters, without confusing them with their digital or visual representations.

boundaries_en: The relation is a cause; idgham and izhar are the ruling that follows from it.
letter_relation.definition_en: The relation of two adjacent letters to each other in point of articulation and attribute: identical, of one kind, close, or distant; the merging of the first into the second, or its clear sounding, is built on it.
letter_relation.purpose_en: Used as a classification tagging the place where two letters are merged or sounded apart, so that the cause of the ruling is known and not only the ruling.

line.definition_en: A typeset line within a page of a mushaf or of a given layout.
line.purpose_en: Used to represent where text and shapes sit within the typeset layout.

boundaries_en: Madani describes the time of revelation, after the Hijrah, not the place of revelation.
madani.definition_en: The part of the Quran revealed after the Hijrah, even where it was revealed outside Madinah.
madani.purpose_en: Used as a value of revelation classification, tagging a surah or an ayah with it.

boundaries_en: The letters of madd are not the letters of lin, though waw and yaa belong to both: a letter of madd is vowelless after the vowel of its own kind, a letter of lin is vowelless after a fathah.
Madd is the ruling; the maddah is the mark that points to it in the mushaf.
madd.definition_en: Prolonging the sound on one of the three letters of madd: a vowelless alif after a fathah, a vowelless waw after a dammah, a vowelless yaa after a kasrah; whether the madd is original, without which the letter does not stand, or secondary, caused by a hamzah or a sukun.
madd.purpose_en: Used as a classification that the kinds of madd branch from, so that a place in the text is tagged with its kind and its length; and because the lengths of the madds are among what differs by tariq, they are part of describing a recording or a mushaf.

madd_al_badal.definition_en: A madd caused by a hamzah before the letter of madd, where the letter of madd was substituted for a vowelless hamzah, as in «آمن», «أوتوا» and «إيمان»; its length is 2 counts for Hafs, more for Warsh.
madd_al_badal.purpose_en: Used as a value of madd, so that a place in the text is tagged with it and with its length, and what differs by tariq is read from it in describing a recording or a mushaf.

madd_al_iwad.definition_en: Lengthening an alif in place of tanwin al-fath when stopping on the word; its length is 2 counts.
madd_al_iwad.purpose_en: Used as a value of madd, so that a place in the text is tagged with it and with its length, and what differs by tariq is read from it in describing a recording or a mushaf.

madd_al_lin.definition_en: Lengthening a vowelless waw or yaa preceded by a fathah when stopping on the word with an incidental sukun, as in «خوف» and «بيت».
madd_al_lin.purpose_en: Used as a value of madd, so that a place in the text is tagged with it and with its length, and what differs by tariq is read from it in describing a recording or a mushaf.

madd_al_silah.definition_en: A madd arising from joining the pronoun haa to a waw or a yaa when it falls between two vowelled letters; sughra when no hamzah follows, kubra when one does.
madd_al_silah.purpose_en: Used as a value of madd, so that a place in the text is tagged with it and with its length, and what differs by tariq is read from it in describing a recording or a mushaf.

madd_arid_li_al_sukun.definition_en: A madd caused by an incidental sukun in stopping after the letter of madd; shortening, middle length and full length are all permitted in it.
madd_arid_li_al_sukun.note_en: The derivation gives `madd_arid_li_al_sukun`, separating the preposition from the article as section 8 requires; the fused form `lilsukun` resolves through `alternative_spellings`.
madd_arid_li_al_sukun.purpose_en: Used as a value of madd, so that a place in the text is tagged with it and with its length, and what differs by tariq is read from it in describing a recording or a mushaf.

madd_lazim.definition_en: A secondary madd caused by an original sukun, fixed in continuing and in stopping, after the letter of madd, in a word or in a letter of the surah openings, whether heavy with idgham or light; its length is 6 counts.
madd_lazim.purpose_en: Used as a value of madd, so that a place in the text is tagged with it and with its length, and what differs by tariq is read from it in describing a recording or a mushaf.

madd_munfasil.definition_en: A secondary madd caused by a hamzah at the start of the word following the letter of madd; it is permissible, shortened or lengthened by riwayah and tariq.
madd_munfasil.purpose_en: Used as a value of madd, so that a place in the text is tagged with it and with its length, and what differs by tariq is read from it in describing a recording or a mushaf.

madd_muttasil.definition_en: A secondary madd caused by a hamzah after the letter of madd within one word; it is obligatory for all the readers, and its lengths differ by riwayah and tariq.
madd_muttasil.purpose_en: Used as a value of madd, so that a place in the text is tagged with it and with its length, and what differs by tariq is read from it in describing a recording or a mushaf.

madd_tabii.definition_en: The madd without which the letter of madd itself does not stand, depending on no cause of hamzah or sukun; its length is 2 counts.
madd_tabii.purpose_en: Used as a value of madd, so that a place in the text is tagged with it and with its length, and what differs by tariq is read from it in describing a recording or a mushaf.

maddah.definition_en: Marks that the letter is lengthened beyond the natural madd.
maddah.purpose_en: Used as a value of the orthographic marks, so that software can tell where the rasm departs from the pronunciation.

boundaries_en: Makki describes the time of revelation, before the Hijrah, not the place of revelation.
makki.definition_en: The part of the Quran revealed before the Hijrah, even where it was revealed outside Makkah.
makki.purpose_en: Used as a value of revelation classification, tagging a surah or an ayah with it.

manzil.definition_en: One of 7 traditional parts of the Quran, made to ease completing it in a week.
manzil.purpose_en: Used in applications that support the manzil system and the reading plans built on it.

mathani.definition_en: The surahs shorter than the miun, coming after them in the traditional division; called mathani because they are recited more often.
mathani.note_en: The standard does not list the group's members surah by surah: the sources differ over the seventh of the tiwal and the start of the mufassal, and no registry yet enumerates each group's members with its source.
mathani.purpose_en: Used as a value of surah group, so that reading plans and the tafsir works that treat the group as a unit can refer to it.

boundaries_en: Meem sakinah is not the meem that noon turns into in iqlab, though the two sound the same.
meem_sakinah.definition_en: A meem carrying no vowel, fixed in pronunciation and in writing, falling in the middle of a word or at its end.
meem_sakinah.purpose_en: Used as the trigger of the three labial rulings, idgham, ikhfa and izhar, in tajwid engines.

miun.definition_en: The surahs whose ayahs come to about 100, a little more or a little less.
miun.note_en: The standard does not list the group's members surah by surah: the sources differ over the seventh of the tiwal and the start of the mufassal, and no registry yet enumerates each group's members with its source.
miun.purpose_en: Used as a value of surah group, so that reading plans and the tafsir works that treat the group as a unit can refer to it.

boundaries_en: A morpheme is a part of a word; a token is a unit of segmentation that may equal a word or span more than one.
morpheme.definition_en: The smallest unit within a word carrying a meaning or a morphological function, such as a prefix, a suffix or a stem.
morpheme.note_en: In Quranic morphology corpora `segment` means the morpheme; in audio APIs it means a word timing. The bare name resolves to nothing, `word_segment` resolves here, and the audio sense is `word_timing`.
morpheme.purpose_en: Used to represent the division of a Quranic word into its morphological parts, which is the level that morphological features and tags are attached to in analysis corpora.

morphology.definition_en: The analysis of a word's structure and form and the morphological properties it carries.
morphology.purpose_en: Used to represent the morphological features of words or tokens.

muallim.definition_en: A recitation style meant for teaching, which may repeat ayahs or leave the learner time to repeat after the reciter.
muallim.purpose_en: Used to classify a recording by its style.

mufassal.definition_en: A group of the short surahs following the mathani; scholars differ over where it begins.
mufassal.note_en: The standard does not list the group's members surah by surah: the sources differ over the seventh of the tiwal and the start of the mufassal, and no registry yet enumerates each group's members with its source.
mufassal.purpose_en: Used as a value of surah group, so that reading plans and the tafsir works that treat the group as a unit can refer to it.

boundaries_en: The mufassir is the one whose statement it is, and his statement may be transmitted in someone else's book.
mufassir.definition_en: One to whom a tafsir of the Quran is attributed, whether by authorship or by transmission.
mufassir.purpose_en: Used to attribute a tafsir to its author, keeping the one who said it apart from the book his words were transmitted in, and from its editor and publisher.

boundaries_en: Mujawwad is a recording style; tajwid is the discipline every style is delivered by. Neither name stands for the other.
mujawwad.definition_en: A recitation style that is slow and melodic, with the tajwid rules drawn out; the label given to recordings delivered that way.
mujawwad.purpose_en: Used to classify a recording by its style.

muqatta_letter.definition_en: Alphabetic letters that open certain surahs, such as Alif Laam Meem, Alif Laam Raa, Haa Meem and Kaaf Haa Yaa Ayn Saad.
muqatta_letter.purpose_en: Used to identify these openings, keep them distinct, and tie them to their surahs and their positions in the text.

muqri.definition_en: One who has received the recitation, mastered it, and transmits it to learners.
muqri.purpose_en: Used to represent the role of teaching, receiving and granting the recitation, which is distinct from being a `reciter`.

boundaries_en: Murattal is a recording style; tartil is a quality of the delivery itself. Neither name stands for the other.
murattal.definition_en: A recitation style that is measured and unadorned, at a reading pace; the label given to recordings delivered that way.
murattal.purpose_en: Used to classify a recording by its style.

boundaries_en: A mushaf is a written vessel for the Quran, not the Quran itself: mushafs differ in rasm, pages and marks while the Quran is one.
mushaf.definition_en: The Quran as a written, bound book, in its established order.
mushaf.purpose_en: Used when the properties of the written representation matter: rasm, layout, pages, lines and marks.

mushaf_edition.definition_en: A specific published edition of the mushaf with its own publisher, rasm, dabt, layout and other properties.
mushaf_edition.purpose_en: Used to tell apart editions that may differ in pages, lines, marks or typographic properties.

mushaf_mark.definition_en: A sign or mark that is not one of a word's original letters, used in the mushaf for reading, organisation or guidance.
mushaf_mark.purpose_en: Gives the different marks one parent, instead of treating them as unrelated kinds.

mutajanisan.definition_en: Two letters of one point of articulation differing in attribute, like the dal and the taa in «قد تبين».
mutajanisan.purpose_en: Used as a value of the relation of two letters, so that the cause of idgham or izhar at the place is read from it rather than worked out from the two letters every time.

mutamathilan.definition_en: Two letters identical in point of articulation and in attribute, like the two baas in «اضرب بعصاك».
mutamathilan.purpose_en: Used as a value of the relation of two letters, so that the cause of idgham or izhar at the place is read from it rather than worked out from the two letters every time.

boundaries_en: The resemblance of wording meant here is not the mutashabih that stands opposite the muhkam in the Quranic sciences.
A resemblance is a relation between two places or more, not a property of a single ayah.
mutashabihat.definition_en: The places in the Quran where the wording of ayahs, or of parts of them, resembles one another, whether exactly or with a slight difference in a word or in order.
mutashabihat.purpose_en: Used above all for memorisation, revision and search tools, since a memoriser needs to know which places are confused with one another and where they differ.

noon_sakinah.definition_en: A noon carrying no vowel, fixed in pronunciation and in writing, in continuing and in stopping.
noon_sakinah.purpose_en: Used as the trigger of the four rulings, izhar, idgham, iqlab and ikhfa, in tajwid engines.

noun.definition_en: A noun in the Arabic sense: a word whose meaning is not tied to a time. Nouns, adjectives, pronouns, demonstratives and relatives are all nouns.
noun.purpose_en: Used as a value of part of speech, and the detailed tags that Quranic morphology corpora use fall under it.

omitted_alif.definition_en: Restores an alif omitted from the Uthmani skeleton but obligatory in pronunciation.
omitted_alif.purpose_en: Used as a value of the orthographic marks, so that software can tell where the rasm departs from the pronunciation.

orthographic_mark.definition_en: A mark fixing how a word is written, such as the hamzah, the maddah and the small letters.
orthographic_mark.purpose_en: Used as the parent of the marks that concern how a word is written, rather than its vowel or how it is stopped on.

page.definition_en: A typographic unit of a given mushaf's layout; its content and its boundaries may differ from one mushaf or edition to another.
page.purpose_en: Used for rendering, navigation and visual alignment according to the pages of a particular mushaf.

part_of_speech.definition_en: The classification of a word or a morpheme by its grammatical class: noun, verb, particle and what branches from them.
part_of_speech.note_en: The threefold division is the level this standard fixes. The detailed tags used by Quranic morphology corpora — dozens of them — are data falling under these three values, and are not given entries of their own in the dictionary.
part_of_speech.purpose_en: Used as the basic tag in morphological and syntactic analysis; searching by tag, filtering, and building the syntactic analysis all rest on it.

boundaries_en: A particle is a part of speech; the written letter, `letter`, is a unit of the written text.
particle.definition_en: A particle: a word with no meaning of its own that gives meaning to the words around it, such as prepositions and the particles of conjunction, negation and interrogation.
particle.purpose_en: Used as a value of part of speech, and the detailed particle tags of Quranic morphology corpora fall under it.

boundaries_en: Qalqalah is one of the attributes of the letters that have no opposite; it counts as a ruling when the place where it appears is tagged with it.
qalqalah.definition_en: A disturbance in the sound of a vowelless letter as it is pronounced, so that a strong beat is heard, in the letters of «قطب جد»; it grows stronger by the letter's place in the word and by stopping on it.
qalqalah.purpose_en: Used as a value of the tajwid ruling, so that a place in the text is tagged with it in analysis, colouring and instruction, and its kinds branch under it in the registry of rulings.

qiraah.definition_en: One of the ways of reciting the Quran, attributed to one of the imams of the qiraat, from which the riwayahs and tariqs branch.
qiraah.purpose_en: Represents the top level of the qiraat model and ties together the riwayahs, the tariqs and the texts bound to them.

qiraah_mark.definition_en: A mark pointing to a particular manner of delivery at its place, such as saktah, ishmam and tashil.
qiraah_mark.purpose_en: Used as the parent of the marks that alert the reader to a particular delivery rather than to the pointing of a letter.

boundaries_en: The Quran is the speech itself; the mushaf is its written vessel. Pages, rasm and marks belong to the mushaf, not to the Quran.
quran.definition_en: The speech of Allah revealed to Muhammad, peace be upon him, whose recitation is worship. The name covers the whole and, by context, any part of it.
quran.purpose_en: Represents the Quranic content itself, independent of any particular mushaf, layout, formatting or digital representation.

boundaries_en: The merit is attached to a place in the Quran; the hadith it comes from is a source it cites, not its location.
Much of what is transmitted about the merits of surahs is weak or fabricated, so it is bound to its source and its grading.
quran_merits.definition_en: What has been transmitted about the merit of the Quran, or of one of its surahs or ayahs, and the reward or effect that follows from reciting it.
quran_merits.purpose_en: Used as content attached to the whole Quran, to a surah or to an ayah. It is kept apart from tafsir because it does not explain meaning, and from hadith because it is organised by place in the text rather than by narrator.

boundaries_en: The rasm is which letters are written, omitted, joined or kept apart; the dabt is the marks of pronunciation placed on the letters.
The script is the shape of the letters in one mushaf; the rasm is what holds in every mushaf written in it.
rasm.definition_en: The way the words of the Quran are written: which letters are written and which omitted or added, and where words are joined or kept apart.
rasm.purpose_en: Used as a classification stating which rasm a text, a mushaf or a dataset is written in, so that search, comparison and rendering branch on it; and it keeps the layer of the rasm distinct from the font, the layout and the drawn glyphs.

boundaries_en: The imlai rasm is a writing and not a reading: the wording is one, and what differs is the form of the word.
The imlai text is not the search text stripped of dabt, though the second is derived from the first.
rasm_imlai.definition_en: Writing the words of the Quran by the rules of modern orthography, writing what the Uthmani rasm omits and omitting what it adds, so that they read in their familiar form.
rasm_imlai.note_en: Deriving the name with the tool gives `orthographic_rasm`, because the general-words table translates «إملائي» to `orthographic` for the sake of «العلامة الإملائية»; the recorded name is `rasm_imlai`, which is what databases and APIs use, and the decision is in the decision record.
rasm_imlai.purpose_en: Used to state that a text follows modern orthography, which is the text that search, quotation and display outside the mushaf are built on, as against the Uthmani text the mushaf is displayed in.

rasm_uthmani.definition_en: The way the words of the Uthmani mushafs are written, with the omission, addition, substitution, separation and joining that go with it.
rasm_uthmani.purpose_en: Used to state that a text follows the rules of the Uthmani rasm rather than another orthography.

boundaries_en: A rawi is the transmitter a riwayah is attributed to; a reciter is the performer of a recording. A performer is not a rawi merely because they recite in his riwayah.
rawi.definition_en: One to whom a transmission from an imam of a qiraah is attributed.
rawi.purpose_en: Used to represent the person a `riwayah` is bound to.

boundaries_en: A recitation is the published recording attributed to a reciter, a riwayah and a style; tilawah is the act.
recitation.definition_en: A published recording of a recitation of the Quran, attributed to a reciter, a riwayah and a style of delivery.
recitation.purpose_en: Used to represent the recording that timings, style and pace are attached to; it is attributed to a reciter and a riwayah and kept apart from the act of tilawah.

recitation_pace.definition_en: A classification of how fast a recitation is delivered while its rules are kept.
recitation_pace.purpose_en: Keeps the traditional paces apart from recording styles such as `murattal` and `mujawwad`.

recitation_style.definition_en: A classification of recordings and recitations by how they are delivered, murattal, mujawwad or muallim, independent of the qiraah and the riwayah.
recitation_style.purpose_en: Used to classify audio recordings by their manner of delivery or by their purpose.

boundaries_en: A reciter performs the recitation in a recording; they are neither an imam of a qiraah nor a rawi.
reciter.definition_en: The person who performs a recitation of the Quran.
reciter.purpose_en: Used to tie audio recordings to their performer.

rectangular_zero.definition_en: Marks an alif dropped in continuation but pronounced when stopping on it.
rectangular_zero.purpose_en: Used as a mark of the mushaf, so that rendering and analysis know where it sits and what it points to.

boundaries_en: Tafsir states the meaning of an ayah by a method; reflection is the effect of that meaning on the one reflecting.
reflection.definition_en: Reflecting on the meanings of the Quran and what they call for in action, and what a reader records of a pause at an ayah or a word.
reflection.purpose_en: Used as content attached to an ayah or to a place within it. It is kept apart from tafsir because it does not undertake to state the apparent meaning, and the one who says it is not necessarily a mufassir.

boundaries_en: Revelation is an event; its order, its classification and its occasion are properties of it, not synonyms for it.
revelation.definition_en: The revelation of the Quran to the Prophet, peace be upon him, in stages over the years of his mission, as events and needs arose.
revelation.purpose_en: Used as the root that the order of revelation, its classification and its occasions branch from: all three are properties of the event of revelation and are known only through it.

revelation_classification.definition_en: A classification of the Quranic text by whether its revelation fell before or after the Hijrah, in the accepted usage.
revelation_classification.purpose_en: Used to classify surahs or ayahs by their relation to the Hijrah, without implying that the classification is only geographical.

boundaries_en: Revelation order is not mushaf order: `surah_number` is the mushaf order.
revelation_order.definition_en: The order of the surahs or the ayahs by the time of their revelation, which may differ from one accepted source to another.
revelation_order.purpose_en: Used to store the order of revelation independently of the order of the mushaf.

riwayah.definition_en: What is attributed to a transmitter from an imam of a qiraah, such as the riwayah of Hafs from Asim.
riwayah.purpose_en: Used to state which riwayah a text, a mushaf, a recording or a dataset follows.

root.definition_en: The morphological origin a word is referred back to, showing its derivation and its relation to other words.
root.purpose_en: Used for morphological search, linguistic analysis, and gathering words that share an origin.

rounded_zero.definition_en: Marks a letter present in the skeleton but never pronounced — neither in continuation nor when stopping.
rounded_zero.purpose_en: Used as a mark of the mushaf, so that rendering and analysis know where it sits and what it points to.

rubu_al_hizb.definition_en: A quarter of a hizb in the well-known division of the mushaf.
rubu_al_hizb.purpose_en: Used to represent the finer division of the hizb and where its marks fall in the mushaf.

ruku.definition_en: A conventional section of the Quran used to organise reading, printed in some mushafs.
ruku.purpose_en: Used in the applications and mushafs that follow the ruku division.

saba_tiwal.definition_en: A group of the longest surahs of the Quran, at its beginning, with a known disagreement over which surah is the seventh.
saba_tiwal.note_en: The standard does not list the group's members surah by surah: the sources differ over the seventh of the tiwal and the start of the mufassal, and no registry yet enumerates each group's members with its source.
saba_tiwal.purpose_en: Used as a value of surah group, so that reading plans and the tafsir works that treat the group as a unit can refer to it.

boundaries_en: The sajdah is the place in the text and the prostration at it, one thing; the sajdah mark is the sign drawn in the mushaf for it.
sajdah.definition_en: A place in the Quran at which the reader and the listener prostrate, ending at a particular ayah. The sajdahs are countable, fifteen by the common count, and some of them are disputed.
sajdah.note_en: Merged from `sajdah_place` and `sujud_al_tilawah`. The dictionary used to keep the place apart from the act; no software stores an act apart from its place, and the common name, "the fifteen sajdahs", names both at once. The reasoning is in the decision record.
sajdah.purpose_en: Used to count the sajdahs, to tie each one to its surah, ayah and page, to attach the rulings and manner of the prostration to it, and to keep it apart from the mark drawn at it.

sajdah_line.definition_en: Marks the word that makes prostration due.
sajdah_line.purpose_en: Used as a mark of the mushaf, so that rendering and analysis know where it sits and what it points to.

boundaries_en: The sajdah mark is a sign in the mushaf; the sajdah is the place in the text at which one prostrates.
sajdah_mark.definition_en: Marks the point at which the reader prostrates.
sajdah_mark.note_en: `alamat_mawdi_al_sajdah` was a separate entry defining the same thing; it was merged into this one.
sajdah_mark.purpose_en: Used as a mark of the mushaf, so that rendering and analysis know where it sits and what it points to.

boundaries_en: The saktah is the pause itself; the saktah mark is the sign drawn in the mushaf for it.
saktah.definition_en: Cutting off the voice for a short moment without breathing, then continuing the recitation.
saktah.purpose_en: Used to represent where a saktah falls and what its properties are in the text or in a recitation.

boundaries_en: The saktah mark is a sign in the mushaf; the saktah is the pause itself.
saktah_mark.definition_en: Marks a saktah: a brief pause without taking a breath, then continuing.
saktah_mark.purpose_en: Used as a value of the qiraah marks, so that the reader is alerted to a particular delivery at its place.

seen_al_qiraah.definition_en: A small seen above a saad marks reading it as seen; below it, reading it as saad.
seen_al_qiraah.purpose_en: Used as a value of the qiraah marks, so that the reader is alerted to a particular delivery at its place.

shaddah.definition_en: Marks a doubled letter: the first, vowelless, is merged into the second and the two are pronounced as one stressed letter.
shaddah.purpose_en: Used as a value of harakah, so that a letter's pronunciation is read from it in analysis, rendering and teaching rather than from the shape of the mark.

small_meem.definition_en: Marks iqlab: a vowelless noon or tanwin pronounced as meem before baa.
small_meem.purpose_en: Used as a mark of the mushaf, so that rendering and analysis know where it sits and what it points to.

small_noon.definition_en: Restores a noon omitted from the skeleton but obligatory in pronunciation, at one place only (21:88).
small_noon.purpose_en: Used as a value of the orthographic marks, so that software can tell where the rasm departs from the pronunciation.

small_waw.definition_en: Marks the silah of the pronoun haa with dammah, pronounced as a waw in continuation.
small_waw.purpose_en: Used as a value of the orthographic marks, so that software can tell where the rasm departs from the pronunciation.

small_yaa.definition_en: Marks the silah of the pronoun haa with kasrah, pronounced as a yaa in continuation.
small_yaa.purpose_en: Used as a value of the orthographic marks, so that software can tell where the rasm departs from the pronunciation.

spoken_translation.definition_en: Rendering the meanings of the Quran into another language in audio or spoken material.
spoken_translation.purpose_en: Used to distinguish audio renderings of the meanings from written translation and from Quranic recitation.

boundaries_en: A root is an abstract derivational origin; a stem is a form that stands in the word once the additions are removed.
stem.definition_en: What remains of a word once its prefixes and suffixes are removed, and what the morphological additions attach to.
stem.purpose_en: Used in morphological analysis as a level between the word form and its root: some corpora record the stem and not the root, and some record both.

sukun.definition_en: Marks a letter that carries no vowel and is articulated clearly.
sukun.purpose_en: Used as a value of harakah, so that a letter's pronunciation is read from it in analysis, rendering and teaching rather than from the shape of the mark.

surah.definition_en: A principal unit of the structure of the Quran, made up of ordered ayahs, with a name and a known place in the order of the mushaf.
surah.purpose_en: Used as the principal unit for organising the text and for attaching ayahs and surah-level data.

surah_group.definition_en: A classification gathering surahs by inherited conventional divisions that rest on length or on their place among the groups of surahs.
surah_group.purpose_en: Gives classifications such as the tiwal, the miun, the mathani and the mufassal one parent.

boundaries_en: The reason for the name concerns the surah's name; the occasion of revelation concerns the revelation of an ayah.
surah_name_reason.definition_en: The statement of why a surah was given its name, and what has been transmitted about it by narration or on linguistic grounds.
surah_name_reason.purpose_en: Used as content attached to a surah. It is kept apart from the occasion of revelation because it concerns the name and not the revelation, and because many surahs have more than one name and so more than one reason.

boundaries_en: The name of a surah is one thing; the reason it was given that name (sabab al-tasmiyah) is another.
The names of a surah are not the names of the Quran itself.
surah_names.definition_en: The names a surah is known by. Most surahs carry more than one: some established by narration, others settled by usage.
surah_names.purpose_en: Used to hold every name a surah is known by, because mushafs differ over the name they print and search must find a surah by any of them.

boundaries_en: A maqsad is an aim that gathers the surah; a topic is one of the things it contains.
surah_objectives.definition_en: The overarching meanings a surah turns on, held together by its subject, and the single aim its ayahs are ordered around.
surah_objectives.purpose_en: Used as content attached to a whole surah rather than to one of its ayahs, which sets it apart from tafsir, which proceeds ayah by ayah, and from a topic index, which lists what the surah contains.

tadwir.definition_en: Reciting at a middle speed between tahqiq and hadr, while keeping the rules.
tadwir.purpose_en: Used as a value of recitation pace, so that a recording or a teaching session is tagged by its pace and filtered by it.

boundaries_en: Tafkhim is an attribute of the letter's sound; istila is the attribute of articulation from which tafkhim follows.
tafkhim.definition_en: A fullness entering the sound of a letter so that the mouth fills with its echo; inherent in the letters of istila, and incidental in the raa, the lam of the name of Allah and the alif, following what precedes them.
tafkhim.purpose_en: Used to tag the places of letters carrying incidental tafkhim in colouring and instruction, and the ranks of tafkhim in the registry of rulings are attributed to it.

tafsir.definition_en: Stating the meanings of the Quran, explaining its wording, and the rulings and guidance it points to, according to the principles of tafsir.
tafsir.purpose_en: Used to represent tafsir works and content and to tie their passages to ayahs, surahs and sources.

boundaries_en: Tafsir al-ray is the statement of its author; tafsir mathur is transmitted with a chain.
tafsir_al_ray.definition_en: Explaining the meanings of the Quran by reasoning and reflection, after knowledge of the speech of the Arabs, its styles and the principles of tafsir, whether the reasoning is approved or censured.
tafsir_al_ray.purpose_en: Used as the kind of authored content attributed to its author as his statement, kept apart from what is transmitted with a chain.

boundaries_en: Tafsir mathur is transmitted with a chain; authored tafsir is the statement of the book's author.
A single report is not a concept in this standard; the concept is the kind of content organised by ayah.
tafsir_mathur.definition_en: Tafsir transmitted with a chain of narration: explanation of the Quran drawn from the Quran itself, from the Sunnah, or from the sayings of the Companions and Successors.
tafsir_mathur.note_en: The better-known title is «التَّفْسِير بِالمَأْثُور», whose derivation fuses the preposition to the noun and gives `tafsir_bialmathur`. The name recorded here is the descriptive form, which is Arabic and in use, and the better-known form resolves through `alternative_spellings`. This is the same reason `abrogation` was given an entry rather than «الناسخ والمنسوخ».
tafsir_mathur.purpose_en: Used as content attached to an ayah and carrying its transmitter and the standing of the transmission with it, so it is not treated as authored tafsir text attributed to a single book.

tahqiq.definition_en: Reciting slowly and deliberately, giving the letters and their rules their full due; much used in teaching.
tahqiq.purpose_en: Used as a value of recitation pace, so that a recording or a teaching session is tagged by its pace and filtered by it.

boundaries_en: Tajwid is a discipline; mujawwad is a recording style. Neither name stands for the other.
tajwid.definition_en: The discipline of delivering the letters of the Quran from their points of articulation and giving them their due properties and rulings.
tajwid.purpose_en: Used as the discipline that tajwid rules, rulings and colour annotations belong to, so that a rule in an engine or a dictionary is attributed to it.

boundaries_en: The ruling is what falls at the place; tajwid is the discipline that settles it.
A ruling is not a rule: the rule is the condition, and the ruling is its effect at the place.
tajwid_ruling.definition_en: What is due in delivering a letter before the letter that follows it, or at a sukun or a hamzah: izhar, idgham, iqlab, ikhfa, madd, qalqalah, tafkhim or tarqiq, as the rules of tajwid settle it at a given place in the text.
tajwid_ruling.purpose_en: Used as the parent of the rulings of tajwid and the holder of their registry, so that the places in the text where a ruling falls are attributed to it, and a particular ruling is named by a row of the registry rather than by a free name that differs from one engine to another.

tanwin.definition_en: An added vowelless noon at the end of a noun, written by doubling the shape of the vowel.
tanwin.purpose_en: Used as the parent of the three tanwin marks, gathering them instead of scattering them through one list.

tanwin_al_damm.definition_en: Marks the un tanwin. Stacked marks signal izhar; staggered marks with a shaddah on the next letter signal complete idgham, and without one, incomplete idgham or ikhfa.
tanwin_al_damm.purpose_en: Used as a value of tanwin, so that the pronunciation of the noun's ending and its ruling are read from it rather than from the shape of the mark.

tanwin_al_fath.definition_en: Marks the an tanwin. Stacked marks signal izhar; staggered marks with a shaddah on the next letter signal complete idgham, and without one, incomplete idgham or ikhfa.
tanwin_al_fath.purpose_en: Used as a value of tanwin, so that the pronunciation of the noun's ending and its ruling are read from it rather than from the shape of the mark.

tanwin_al_kasr.definition_en: Marks the in tanwin. Stacked marks signal izhar; staggered marks with a shaddah on the next letter signal complete idgham, and without one, incomplete idgham or ikhfa.
tanwin_al_kasr.purpose_en: Used as a value of tanwin, so that the pronunciation of the noun's ending and its ruling are read from it rather than from the shape of the mark.

tariq.definition_en: A path of transmission taken from a rawi through those below him in the chain of transmission of a qiraah.
tariq.note_en: The four named routes applications store — shatibiyyah, tayyibat_al_nashr, durrah, taysir — are in `registries/tariq.tsv`; the full enumeration, some 980 turuq of al-Nashr, is still open.
tariq.purpose_en: Used when data needs a finer level than the riwayah to tell paths of delivery and transmission apart.

tarqiq.definition_en: A thinness entering the sound of a letter so that the mouth does not fill with its echo; inherent in the letters of istifal, and incidental in the raa and the lam of the name of Allah.
tarqiq.purpose_en: Used to tag the places of letters carrying incidental tarqiq in colouring and instruction, as the counterpart of tafkhim.

boundaries_en: Tartil is a quality of the delivery itself; murattal is a recording style. Neither name stands for the other.
tartil.definition_en: Reciting the Quran deliberately, making the letters and words distinct, observing the stops and the meaning.
tartil.purpose_en: Used as a quality of delivery in describing a recording or a lesson, not as the name of the style a recording is published under.

tashil.definition_en: Marks tashil: the hamzah softened to a sound between a hamzah and an alif.
tashil.purpose_en: Used as a value of the qiraah marks, so that the reader is alerted to a particular delivery at its place.

boundaries_en: Tashkil is the layer; a harakah is one mark.
Dabt is the discipline and its rules; tashkil is what it produces on the letters.
tashkil.definition_en: The layer of dabt marks attached to the letters of the text, the harakat, tanwin, shaddah, sukun and what goes with them, taken as a whole.
tashkil.purpose_en: Used when the whole layer of dabt is handled at once, kept in display or stripped from the text for search, rather than one mark.

three_dots.definition_en: Three dots above the letter, distinguishing it from the others that share its skeleton (ijam): thaa, sheen.
three_dots.purpose_en: Used as a value of ijam, so that a letter is told apart from those sharing its skeleton in analysis and in search.

thumn.definition_en: An eighth of a hizb, a division used in some mushafs and schools.
thumn.purpose_en: Used when supporting sources or mushafs that divide the hizb into eighths.

boundaries_en: Tilawah is the act; `recitation` is the published recording attributed to a reciter, a riwayah and a style of delivery.
Tartil is an attribute of tilawah, not tilawah.
tilawah.definition_en: Reading the Quran in its wording, delivered aloud as the reader received it, whether in prayer, in a lesson or in a recording.
tilawah.purpose_en: Used for the act of reading itself where that is what is meant, as in the rulings of tilawah, its etiquette, its prostration and its teaching; the published recording of it stays `recitation`.

boundaries_en: A word is a unit the reader recognises; a token is a unit a segmentation method produces, so changing the method changes the number of tokens and not the number of words.
token.definition_en: A unit produced by segmenting the text according to a declared method. It may equal a word, be part of one, or span more than one.
token.purpose_en: Used to tie automated analysis to the text where the word boundary is not the segmentation boundary, and to keep what a segmenter produces distinct from what a reader counts as a word.

translation.definition_en: Rendering the meanings of the Quran into another language. A translation is not the Quran in its wording.
translation.purpose_en: Used to tie translated-meaning texts to ayahs, languages, translators and sources.

boundaries_en: The translator is not the mufassir, though the translation may rest on a tafsir.
translator.definition_en: One to whom a translation of the meanings of the Quran into another language is attributed, whether a person or a body.
translator.purpose_en: Used to attribute a translation to its author, keeping the author apart from the publisher, the reviewer and the source of the text.

transliteration.definition_en: Representing the letters of one writing system with those of another by fixed rules, without translating the meaning.
transliteration.purpose_en: Used to give a readable representation in another writing system, or for systematic conversion between writing systems.

two_dots.definition_en: Two dots, above or below, distinguishing a letter from the others that share its skeleton (ijam): taa, yaa, qaaf.
two_dots.purpose_en: Used as a value of ijam, so that a letter is told apart from those sharing its skeleton in analysis and in search.

verb.definition_en: A verb: a word whose meaning is tied to a time, with past, present and imperative forms.
verb.purpose_en: Used as a value of part of speech, and the morphological features specific to verbs — tense, voice and pattern — hang off it.

boundaries_en: A wajh does not change what the reading is attributed to; a tariq does.
wajh.definition_en: One of several manners of delivery, any of which may be taken within one riwayah or one tariq, such as the wajhs of madd arid li al-sukun.
wajh.purpose_en: Used when a recording or a lesson needs to state which of the permitted wajhs was taken, without attributing the difference to a riwayah or a tariq.

waqf.definition_en: Stopping the recitation at a place in the text according to the rules of stopping and starting.
waqf.purpose_en: Represents the general concept of stopping, while `waqf_mark` represents the printed signs that point to it.

waqf_al_muanaqah.definition_en: Two candidate stopping points: stopping at one makes stopping at the other not allowed.
waqf_al_muanaqah.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf mark type, so that rendering, teaching and warnings in applications branch on it rather than on the shape of the sign.

waqf_hasan.definition_en: A stop that yields a meaning but is connected to what follows it in wording and in meaning.
waqf_hasan.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf ruling, so that a place is tagged with it in teaching and analysis.

waqf_jaiz_mustawi_al_tarafayn.definition_en: A permissible stop, with stopping and continuing equally sound.
waqf_jaiz_mustawi_al_tarafayn.note_en: `waqf_jaiz` was this mark's id in the mushaf registry; it fits three permissible marks, so it is deprecated.
waqf_jaiz_mustawi_al_tarafayn.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf mark type, so that rendering, teaching and warnings in applications branch on it rather than on the shape of the sign.

waqf_jaiz_waqf_awla.arabic: الوَقْف الجَائِز مَعَ كَوْنِ الوَقْف أَوْلَى
waqf_jaiz_waqf_awla.definition_en: A permissible stop, and stopping is the better choice.
waqf_jaiz_waqf_awla.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf mark type, so that rendering, teaching and warnings in applications branch on it rather than on the shape of the sign.

waqf_jaiz_wasl_awla.arabic: الوَقْف الجَائِز مَعَ كَوْنِ الوَصْل أَوْلَى
waqf_jaiz_wasl_awla.definition_en: A permissible stop, but continuing is the better choice.
waqf_jaiz_wasl_awla.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf mark type, so that rendering, teaching and warnings in applications branch on it rather than on the shape of the sign.

waqf_kafi.definition_en: A stop whose meaning is complete but which is connected to what follows it in meaning, not in wording.
waqf_kafi.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf ruling, so that a place is tagged with it in teaching and analysis.

waqf_lazim.definition_en: A compulsory stop: continuing across it would suggest a meaning other than the one intended.
waqf_lazim.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf mark type, so that rendering, teaching and warnings in applications branch on it rather than on the shape of the sign.

waqf_mamnu.definition_en: A forbidden stop: stopping here would break the meaning or attach what follows to the wrong clause.
waqf_mamnu.note_en: Registered in the mushaf registry but never used in this edition: zero occurrences.
waqf_mamnu.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf mark type, so that rendering, teaching and warnings in applications branch on it rather than on the shape of the sign.

waqf_mark.definition_en: A mark in the mushaf pointing the reader to the ruling on stopping or continuing at a given place.
waqf_mark.purpose_en: Used to represent the sign, its position and its type in an orderly way.

boundaries_en: The mark type is what a drawn mark points to; the waqf ruling belongs to the place itself, even where no mark is drawn on it.
waqf_mark_type.definition_en: A classification of what a waqf mark drawn in the mushaf points to: that stopping is compulsory, forbidden or permitted.
waqf_mark_type.purpose_en: Gives applications one set of values to branch on, instead of reading the shape of the sign itself.

waqf_qabih.definition_en: A stop that yields no meaning, or yields a meaning that is not the one intended.
waqf_qabih.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf ruling, so that a place is tagged with it in teaching and analysis.

boundaries_en: The waqf ruling belongs to the place; the waqf mark type is what a drawn mark points to, and a place may have a ruling with no mark on it.
waqf_ruling.definition_en: A classification of the place itself by whether the meaning is complete there, not of the mark drawn at it.
waqf_ruling.purpose_en: Used in teaching and in the syntactic and semantic analysis of stopping.

waqf_tamm.definition_en: A stop whose meaning is complete and which is connected to what follows it neither in wording nor in meaning.
waqf_tamm.purpose_en: Used as a value of the waqf ruling, so that a place is tagged with it in teaching and analysis.

boundaries_en: A word is a unit the reader recognises; a token is a unit a segmentation method produces, so changing the method changes the number of tokens and not the number of words.
word.definition_en: A unit of the text that a reader recognises as one word, independent of how a segmenter splits the text.
word.purpose_en: Used to attach word-level data: root, morphology, irab, tajwid, audio alignment and visual position.

boundaries_en: The translation of a word on its own is not a translation of the ayah, and is not shown in its place.
word_by_word_translation.definition_en: A translation giving each word of the ayah its meaning in another language on its own, in the order of the original words.
word_by_word_translation.purpose_en: Used in instructional display and in learning, and attached to the word by its key rather than to the ayah.

boundaries_en: The position in the key is the word's, not the token's; changing the segmentation method that counts the words changes the key.
word_key.definition_en: A textual identifier of a word that adds the word's position within the ayah to the ayah key, in the form `2:255:5`; the position is counted from the start of the ayah by a declared segmentation method.
word_key.purpose_en: Used as the key for data attached to the word: timing, word-by-word translation, morphological analysis and images.

boundaries_en: Gharib al-Quran explains a word; tafsir explains the meaning of an ayah.
The meaning is attributed to a particular book, so it may differ between sources.
word_meanings.definition_en: The explanation of Quranic words whose meaning is obscure to most readers, whether because they are rare in use or because their sense has shifted.
word_meanings.purpose_en: Used as content attached to a particular word of an ayah rather than to the whole ayah, which is what sets it apart from tafsir and its explanation of the ayah's overall meaning.

boundaries_en: A word timing falls inside the timing of its ayah and does not cross it.
Audio APIs call this concept `segment`; the name in this standard is `word_timing`, because in linguistic corpora `segment` names the morpheme.
word_timing.definition_en: A span of time in a recitation recording, given by a start and an end, corresponding to one word of an ayah.
word_timing.purpose_en: Used to highlight the word being recited while listening, to align text with audio at a level finer than the ayah, and to cut a recording at a word.
